subject: Dedicated capacity incident: fallback actions, customer update, and postmortem link
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity incident — immediate update and mitigations

Hi Aisha,

I wanted to follow up with an immediate status update on the capacity issues you saw this morning (we detected elevated tail latency and failed allocations for your dedicated GPU pool). Brief summary:

- What happened: an autoscaler regression caused several GPU hosts to be marked unhealthy during a rolling upgrade, which reduced available capacity and caused backlog on your pool.
- Impact: increased request latency for a minority of requests and a small number of short-lived errors (~2.3% of calls during the window).
- Actions taken: we paused the rolling upgrade, manually scaled up the pool by adding two spare nodes, and temporarily routed non-critical requests to a compatible lower-memory model to preserve latency for user-facing paths.

We know this affected your production inference. We're preparing a formal postmortem and a review of our rollout safety checks; draft is attached. We will provide usage offsets for any customer-facing impact and a proposed credit.

Immediate asks for you: can you confirm if you saw any business-critical failures we should prioritize in the remediation? Also tell me the best time tomorrow for a brief 30-minute sync to walk through the timeline and next steps.

Apologies for the disruption — we own this and will make sure you have the information and mitigation steps you need.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf (11 pages), usage-offsets.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 15:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity incident — immediate update and mitigations

Thanks for the quick update, Jonas.

We saw increased latency on our inference endpoint between 10:52–11:34 PST; some inference jobs timed out and triggered downstream retries in our pipeline. The percentage of failed jobs was small but one of them was part of a scheduled nightly batch; that led to a delayed report for a partner.

Questions:
- Can you share the exact allocation window and the hosts that were drained? We need the logs to correlate with our internal retry behavior.
- What credit are you proposing for the disrupted usage?
- Tomorrow at 11:00am PST for a 30-min call works for our ops lead.

Appreciate the transparency.

—Aisha
VP of Engineering, Acme Analytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:12:10 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme incident — timeline + artifacts to collect

Evelyn / Dylan,

Following Aisha's note, please take the following action items before our customer call at 11:00am PST tomorrow: 

1) Evelyn: pull health-check and autoscaler logs for the pool between 10:30–12:00 PST on 2026-05-03. Include node IDs and hostnames and mark which ones were involved in the rolling upgrade. We need the exact allocation window for the customer.
2) Dylan: prepare a short runbook note on why we routed to the lower-memory model and confirm any model-compatibility differences (tokenization, response format) that Acme might have seen. Also compute the usage offsets and a proposed credit range (suggest 5–12% depending on their impacted workload). Put the numbers into usage-offsets.xlsx (attached to the thread).
3) Draft a concise postmortem (one-pager timeline + root cause + mitigation + owner and ETA). Attach to the external follow-up.

I'll coordinate the customer call and lead the external summary. Keep me posted in this thread and paste any Drive links here.

Jonas
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up and final postmortem snapshot — Dedicated capacity incident (May 3)

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the sync earlier today. Below is the customer-facing summary plus links to artifacts.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: a regression in the autoscaler health-evaluation logic combined with an in-flight orchestration rollout caused 3 host health checks to be mis-classified as degraded. The misclassification triggered host remediation and temporary capacity loss for your dedicated pool.
- Impact: Elevated latency and transient errors for ~2.3% of calls to your pool between 2026-05-03T10:52:00-07:00 and 2026-05-03T11:34:00-07:00. Affected sessions were mostly longer-context inference jobs; we have identified log traces that map to the timestamps you provided.
- Mitigation & permanent fixes:
  - Immediate: paused the rollout, manually added two spare GPU hosts, and routed lower-priority traffic to a compatible, lower-memory model to preserve critical latency SLAs.
  - Short-term fix (in progress, ETA 2026-05-12): revert the autoscaler regression and add an additional safety check on host health transitions.
  - Long-term (ETA Q3 2026): improved rollout gating including canary scheduling tied to real-time allocation metrics and an autoscaler refactor to decouple health evaluation from orchestration events.

Artifacts and evidence:
- Postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/postmortems/ACME-7542-dedicated-2026-05 (PDF attached).
- Host allocation list and health-check logs: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/postmortems/ACME-7542-dedicated-2026-05/host-logs.csv
- Usage offsets and proposed credit: usage-offsets.xlsx (attached). Proposed credit: 8% of billed usage during the affected window; we discussed flexibility and Acme's ops constraints on the call.

Next steps we committed to on the call:
- [Jonas] Deliver the finalized postmortem (one-pager + full timeline) by 2026-05-07.
- [Evelyn] Deliver cleaned host logs and a short verification script by 2026-05-06 so Acme can reproduce mapping to their job IDs.
- [Dylan] Ship the autoscaler revert and safety check in a controlled patch (canary -> roll) by 2026-05-12.

Please reply here if you'd like any additional artifacts. If the proposed credit is acceptable I will route the bill adjustment through our billing operations.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate your partnership and will update you as we close the action items.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf, usage-offsets.xlsx
